cards.front:
The Employees' Provident Fund & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 applies to every factory or
establishment employing:

(A) 10 or more persons
(B) 20 or more persons
(C) 50 or more persons
(D) 100 or more persons
cards.back:
(B) 20 or more persons

II.4 Applicability — S.1(3)(a): EPF Act applies to every establishment employing 20 or more persons. Central Govt may extend to establishments with <20 by notification in Official Gazette.

cards.front:
Which of the following establishments can be brought under EPF Act by notification even if they
employ fewer than 20 persons?

(A) Factories employing contract labour
(B) Establishments notified under S.1(3)(b)
(C) Shops under Shops & Establishments Act only
(D) Sole proprietorships only
cards.back:
(B) Establishments notified under S.1(3)(b)

II.4 Applicability — S.1(3)(b) empowers Central Govt to notify any establishment for coverage with at least 2 months' prior notice in the Official Gazette.

cards.front:
A factory once covered under EPF Act ceases to be covered when the employee strength falls
below 20. True or False?

(A) True, it is automatically de-covered
(B) False — once covered, always covered (S.1(5))
(C) True only if fall persists for 12 months
(D) True only with Central Govt approval
cards.back:
(B) False — once covered, always covered (S.1(5))

II.4 Applicability — S.1(5): 'An establishment to which this Act applies shall continue to be governed by this Act notwithstanding that the number of persons employed therein at any time falls below 20.'

cards.front:
The EPF Act does NOT apply to:

(A) Co-operative societies employing less than 50 persons and working without power
(B) Private limited companies
(C) LLPs with 25 employees
(D) Charitable trusts running hospitals
cards.back:
(A) Co-operative societies employing less than 50 persons and working without power

II.4 Applicability — Co-operatives with <50 workers operating without the aid of power are specifically excluded under S.16(1)(a). They can, however, opt to join voluntarily.

cards.front:
The wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage of a new joiner is currently:

(A) ₹6,500 per month
(B) ₹15,000 per month
(C) ₹21,000 per month
(D) ₹25,000 per month ■ II.4 Definitions
cards.back:
(B) ₹15,000 per month

II.4 Applicability — Wage ceiling was raised from ₹6,500 to ₹15,000 w.e.f. 1 September 2014. An employee earning >₹15,000 at joining can still opt in jointly with employer.

cards.front:
'Basic wages' under S.2(b) of EPF Act excludes which of the following?

(A) Dearness allowance
(B) House rent allowance
(C) Overtime allowance
(D) All of the above
cards.back:
(D) All of the above

II.4 Definitions — S.2(b) excludes DA, HRA, overtime, bonus, commission, presents from employer from basic wages definition — though DA IS added for contribution computation under S.6.

cards.front:
In Bridge & Roof Co. vs Union of India (1963), the Supreme Court held that for inclusion in basic
wages, an allowance must be:

(A) Paid on festival occasions only
(B) Universally, necessarily and ordinarily paid to all workmen
(C) Paid to managerial staff only
(D) Paid only during peak season
cards.back:
(B) Universally, necessarily and ordinarily paid to all workmen

II.4 Definitions — Bridge & Roof (1963) laid the 'universally, ordinarily and necessarily paid' test for identifying basic wages, later reaffirmed in Surya Roshni (2019).

cards.front:
In Surya Roshni Ltd vs EPFO (28 Feb 2019), the Supreme Court held:

(A) EPFO cannot recover past dues
(B) Variable allowances paid to all workers are part of basic wages
(C) Piece-rated wages are excluded from EPF
(D) EPS-95 is unconstitutional ■ II.5 Contributions
cards.back:
(B) Variable allowances paid to all workers are part of basic wages

II.4 Definitions — Surya Roshni held that special allowances which are universally paid to all employees are 'basic wages' and hence attract PF contribution. Burden of proof on the employer. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
The rate of employee's contribution to EPF (standard rate) is:

(A) 10% of basic wages + DA
(B) 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance
(C) 8.33% of basic wages
(D) 6.5% of basic wages
cards.back:
(B) 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance

II.5 Contributions — S.6: Employee contributes 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance. Employer matches 12%.

cards.front:
Out of the employer's 12% contribution, what percentage is diverted to EPS 1995?

(A) 3.67%
(B) 8.33%
(C) 10%
(D) 12%
cards.back:
(B) 8.33%

II.5 Contributions — Employer's 12% is split: 8.33% → EPS (capped at ₹1,250 on ₹15,000 wage); 3.67% → EPF. If wages exceed ₹15,000, entire EPS share goes if higher-pension option exercised.

cards.front:
For certain notified establishments the contribution rate is reduced from 12% to:

(A) 6%
(B) 8%
(C) 10%
(D) 11%
cards.back:
(C) 10%

II.5 Contributions — 10% rate applies under S.6 proviso to: establishments with <20 employees declared as sick, those in five specified industries (jute, beedi, brick, coir, guar gum), and certain others.

cards.front:
Government of India's contribution to EPS 1995 is:

(A) Nil
(B) 1.16% of wages up to the wage ceiling
(C) 2% of basic wages
(D) 3.67% of basic wages
cards.back:
(B) 1.16% of wages up to the wage ceiling

II.5 Contributions — The Central Government contributes 1.16% of wages (capped at ₹15,000) to EPS, making the total EPS contribution equal to 8.33% + 1.16% = 9.49% of capped wages.

cards.front:
The administrative charges paid by the employer to EPF (since 1-Jun-2018) are:

(A) 0.01%
(B) 0.5%
(C) 0.65%
(D) 1.10%
cards.back:
(B) 0.5%

II.5 Contributions — EPF admin charges have been 0.5% of EPF wages since 1 June 2018 (minimum ₹500/month, or ₹75 for non-functional establishments). Earlier 1.10%, then 0.65%. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
The EDLI administrative charges payable by employer are:

(A) Nil
(B) 0.01%
(C) 0.5%
(D) 1.10%
cards.back:
(B) 0.01%

II.5 Contributions — EDLI admin charges are 0.01% (minimum ₹200/month) since April 2017.

cards.front:
EPF interest rate declared for FY 2025-26 (239th CBT) is:

(A) 8.00%
(B) 8.10%
(C) 8.25%
(D) 8.50%
cards.back:
(C) 8.25%

II.5 Contributions — 239th CBT retained 8.25% for FY 2025-26 — third consecutive year. Needs MoF concurrence; credited June-Aug 2026.

cards.front:
Which body recommends the EPF interest rate annually?

(A) RBI
(B) Ministry of Labour
(C) Central Board of Trustees (CBT)
(D) Finance Commission
cards.back:
(C) Central Board of Trustees (CBT)

II.5 Contributions — CBT is the supreme policy body under S.5A. It recommends; MoF concurs; then credited.

cards.front:
The interest on EPF accumulations is credited:

(A) Monthly in arrears
(B) Quarterly
(C) Half-yearly
(D) Annually after MoF approval
cards.back:
(D) Annually after MoF approval

II.5 Contributions — Interest is declared annually by CBT, approved by MoF, and credited retrospectively to each member's account for the relevant financial year.

cards.front:
A member's EPF account becomes INOPERATIVE (no further interest credit) after:

(A) 1 year from last contribution
(B) 3 years of cessation with no claim
(C) 36 months from cessation — earlier rule, now withdrawn
(D) Never — interest accrues till 58 ■ II.6 CBT Structure
cards.back:
(D) Never — interest accrues till 58 ■ II.6 CBT Structure

II.5 Contributions — Since 2016, interest is credited on inoperative accounts too, till member attains 58 years of age, reversing the earlier '36-month stop' rule.

cards.front:
The Central Board of Trustees (CBT) is constituted under which section of EPF Act?

(A) Section 5
(B) Section 5A
(C) Section 5B
(D) Section 5C
cards.back:
(B) Section 5A

II.6 CBT Structure — S.5A constitutes CBT as a tripartite body — Central Govt + State Govts + employers + employees.

cards.front:
Chairman of CBT is:

(A) RBI Governor
(B) Labour Secretary
(C) Union Labour Minister (nominated by Central Govt)
(D) Central PF Commissioner
cards.back:
(C) Union Labour Minister (nominated by Central Govt)

II.6 CBT Structure — Union Minister of Labour & Employment is the ex-officio Chairman of CBT.

cards.front:
CPFC (Central Provident Fund Commissioner) functions as:

(A) Chairman of CBT
(B) Member-Secretary and CEO of CBT
(C) Advisor without voting right
(D) Chief Justice of EPFAT ■ II.7 Offences & Penalties
cards.back:
(B) Member-Secretary and CEO of CBT

II.6 CBT Structure — CPFC is the Member-Secretary of CBT and Chief Executive of EPFO. He implements CBT decisions.

cards.front:
Default in payment of employee's EPF contribution deducted from wages is punishable under:

(A) S.14(1A) — imprisonment 1-3 years + fine ₹10,000
(B) S.14(1B) — imprisonment 1-3 years + fine ₹5,000
(C) S.14AA only
(D) S.10 — priority provisions
cards.back:
(A) S.14(1A) — imprisonment 1-3 years + fine ₹10,000

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14(1A): Default in deducted contributions = imprisonment 1-3 years (min 1 year) + fine ₹10,000 mandatory. Higher punishment than default in employer's own share.

cards.front:
Under S.14(1) of EPF Act, making a false statement or representation attracts:

(A) Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹5,000 or both
(B) Imprisonment up to 3 years without fine
(C) Only administrative penalty
(D) Only civil suit
cards.back:
(A) Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹5,000 or both

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14(1): false statement = up to 1 year jail or fine up to ₹5,000 or both.

cards.front:
Section 14B of EPF Act empowers the authority to levy:

(A) Compensation
(B) Damages for delayed payment of contributions
(C) Interest on arrears
(D) Criminal fine
cards.back:
(B) Damages for delayed payment of contributions

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14B authorises levy of damages for default in payment, separate from interest under S.7Q.

cards.front:
Post 15 June 2024, damages under S.14B / Para 32A are levied at:

(A) 5-25% per annum on slab basis
(B) Uniform 1% per month (12% per annum) with no cap
(C) 0.5% per month flat
(D) Central Govt-discretion rate
cards.back:
(B) Uniform 1% per month (12% per annum) with no cap

II.7 Offences & Penalties — Amendment dated 14 June 2024 (effective 15 June 2024) made damages a uniform 1% per month (12% p.a.) with no upper cap, replacing the older slab-rate (17-37% max).

cards.front:
Interest payable under Section 7Q of EPF Act for delayed deposit of contribution is:

(A) 1% p.a.
(B) 6% p.a.
(C) 12% p.a.
(D) 18% p.a.
cards.back:
(C) 12% p.a.

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.7Q prescribes simple interest at 12% per annum from due date till date of actual payment. This is independent of S.14B damages.

cards.front:
Which of the following is TRUE about S.7Q interest?

(A) It requires a separate quasi-judicial order
(B) It is automatic and payable on default
(C) It is discretionary
(D) It is chargeable only if delay exceeds 60 days
cards.back:
(B) It is automatic and payable on default

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.7Q interest is automatic and does not require a show-cause notice — pure arithmetical charge. Unlike S.14B damages, no discretion or enquiry is required.

cards.front:
Repeat offences under EPF Act (S.14AA) are punishable with:

(A) Same sentence as first offence
(B) Enhanced imprisonment (up to 5 years)
(C) Only monetary fine
(D) Debarment from tenders ■ II.8 7A Enquiry
cards.back:
(B) Enhanced imprisonment (up to 5 years)

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14AA: enhanced imprisonment of not less than 2 years but may extend to 5 years + fine not less than ₹25,000 for repeat offences.

cards.front:
A Section 7A enquiry is conducted by an officer of which rank or higher?

(A) Enforcement Officer
(B) Assistant PF Commissioner (APFC)
(C) Additional Central PF Commissioner
(D) Only a civil judge
cards.back:
(B) Assistant PF Commissioner (APFC)

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A empowers Central PF Commissioner and officers notified — APFC and above are authorised. EO/AO cannot conduct 7A enquiries. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
Which of the following civil-court powers is available to a S.7A officer?

(A) Enforcing attendance of witnesses
(B) Compelling production of documents
(C) Issuing commissions for examination of witnesses
(D) All of the above
cards.back:
(D) All of the above

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A(2) vests powers of civil court under CPC for: (a) enforcing attendance, (b) requiring document production, (c) issuing commissions, (d) receiving evidence on affidavit.

cards.front:
A 7A order must be:

(A) Oral
(B) A speaking order — recording reasons
(C) Unreasoned (discretionary)
(D) Anonymous
cards.back:
(B) A speaking order — recording reasons

II.8 7A Enquiry — The order must be a speaking order, giving reasons (principles of natural justice). This principle flows from Articles 14/21 & S.7A(2) civil-court powers.

cards.front:
Review of a S.7A order can be sought under:

(A) Section 7A itself
(B) Section 7B
(C) Section 7C
(D) Section 7Q
cards.back:
(B) Section 7B

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7B allows review of 7A orders on grounds like error apparent on the face of the record, discovery of new evidence, etc. Appeal lies to CGIT under S.7I.

cards.front:
Appeal from a S.7A order lies to:

(A) High Court directly
(B) Central Government Industrial Tribunal (CGIT)
(C) Supreme Court
(D) District Judge
cards.back:
(B) Central Government Industrial Tribunal (CGIT)

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7I: appeal lies to the Central Government Industrial Tribunal (also called EPFAT). Pre-deposit of 75% of determined dues required under S.7O.

cards.front:
Pre-deposit requirement for an appeal to CGIT under S.7O is:

(A) 25% of the dues determined
(B) 50% of the dues determined
(C) 75% of the dues determined
(D) 100% of the dues determined ■ II.9 Inspector Powers
cards.back:
(C) 75% of the dues determined

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7O requires 75% pre-deposit of determined amount (Tribunal may waive/reduce for hardship).

cards.front:
Inspector powers under EPF Act flow from:

(A) Section 12
(B) Section 13
(C) Section 14
(D) Section 15
cards.back:
(B) Section 13

II.9 Inspector Powers — S.13 empowers appointment of Inspectors and prescribes their powers — search, examination, calling for records etc.

cards.front:
Which of the following is NOT an Inspector's power under S.13?

(A) Enter premises at reasonable times
(B) Seize records indefinitely without limit
(C) Examine employer or employees
(D) Require production of books of account
cards.back:
(B) Seize records indefinitely without limit

II.9 Inspector Powers — Seizure by inspector is subject to limits; records must be examined and copies taken — indefinite retention without cause is not permitted.

cards.front:
Obstruction of an Inspector under S.13 is an offence punishable under:

(A) S.14(1)
(B) S.14(2) — imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹4,000
(C) S.14A
(D) S.14B
cards.back:
(B) S.14(2) — imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to ₹4,000

II.9 Inspector Powers — S.14(2) makes obstruction of or failure to comply with Inspector's requisition punishable.

cards.front:
Under S.12 of EPF Act, an employer:

(A) Can recover employee contribution from wages without restriction
(B) Cannot reduce wages of an employee merely because of liability under the Act
(C) Can suspend employee for non-contribution
(D) Is always liable for interest on delay ■ II.5 Contributions
cards.back:
(B) Cannot reduce wages of an employee merely because of liability under the Act

II.9 Inspector Powers — S.12 prohibits reduction of wages (or any compensation) by the employer merely to counter his EPF contribution liability — protects employees from indirect pass-through. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
Which paragraph of EPF Scheme 1952 governs damages?

(A) Para 30
(B) Para 32
(C) Para 32A
(D) Para 72
cards.back:
(C) Para 32A

II.5 Contributions — Para 32A (amended 14 Jun 2024) lays down the uniform 1% per month damages structure.

cards.front:
Which paragraph governs voluntary withdrawal from EPF?

(A) Para 60
(B) Para 68
(C) Para 72
(D) Para 76
cards.back:
(C) Para 72

II.5 Contributions — Para 72 of EPF Scheme governs settlement of accounts on retirement, death, or after 2 months unemployment.

cards.front:
An EPF member below 58 years can make NON-refundable withdrawal for which of the
following?

(A) Marriage of self/siblings/children
(B) Education of self/children
(C) Purchase or construction of house
(D) All of the above
cards.back:
(D) All of the above

II.5 Contributions — Para 68-B, 68-K, etc. permit partial NON-refundable withdrawals for housing, marriage, education, medical treatment, and some other specified contingencies.

cards.front:
A member can withdraw entire EPF balance if continuously unemployed for:

(A) 1 month
(B) 2 months
(C) 6 months
(D) 1 year
cards.back:
(B) 2 months

II.5 Contributions — Para 69 (pre-Oct 2025 rule): after 2 months → 100% withdrawable. Post 13-Oct-2025 CBT: 75% immediate; remaining 25% only after 12 months continuous unemployment. After 1 month: 75% advance (post-Covid rule).

cards.front:
The wage ceiling for EDLI and EPS mandatory coverage is:

(A) ₹6,500
(B) ₹15,000
(C) ₹21,000
(D) ₹25,000
cards.back:
(B) ₹15,000

II.5 Contributions — Both EPS and EDLI use the ₹15,000 wage ceiling. EDLI's insurance benefit also uses capped wage.

cards.front:
Which category of workers was universally added to EPF coverage by Code-period
amendments?

(A) Gig and platform workers (under SS Code)
(B) Only software engineers
(C) Only public sector workers
(D) Only apprentices
cards.back:
(A) Gig and platform workers (under SS Code)

II.5 Contributions — SS Code 2020 expanded social security coverage to gig and platform workers — administered through a new Social Security Fund.

cards.front:
Once a member crosses age 58, what happens to EPS contribution?

(A) Continues as before
(B) Stops; entire 12% of employer goes to EPF
(C) Goes to pension fund as before
(D) Member must retire
cards.back:
(B) Stops; entire 12% of employer goes to EPF

II.5 Contributions — On attaining age 58, EPS contribution stops. Thereafter, the full 12% employer share goes to EPF. Monthly pension starts (subject to eligibility).

cards.front:
Interest on EPF is compounded:

(A) Daily
(B) Monthly
(C) Yearly on running monthly balance
(D) Quarterly ■ II.8 7A Enquiry
cards.back:
(C) Yearly on running monthly balance

II.5 Contributions — Interest is credited annually but calculated on the running monthly balance (so effectively compounded yearly).

cards.front:
Limitation for initiating a S.7A enquiry is:

(A) 3 years
(B) 5 years
(C) No express limitation under EPF Act
(D) 12 years
cards.back:
(C) No express limitation under EPF Act

II.8 7A Enquiry — No express period of limitation for S.7A. However, courts have held delay must be explained (doctrine of reasonableness). Post Vivekananda (SC 2019), EPFO issued 14-Feb-2020 guidelines curbing 'roving' 7A notices.

cards.front:
Which of the following orders is made by the 7A officer after hearing?

(A) Determining amount due from employer
(B) Adjusting inter-member transfers
(C) Cancelling EPF allotment number
(D) Passing detention order ■ II.9 Recovery
cards.back:
(A) Determining amount due from employer

II.8 7A Enquiry — S.7A is specifically to determine the amount due from an employer (arrears of contribution, interest, damages sometimes clubbed in same proceedings via composite SCN).

cards.front:
Recovery of EPF dues under Section 8 is NOT made through which of the following modes?

(A) Attachment and sale of property
(B) Arrest and detention
(C) Appointment of a receiver
(D) Attachment of movable property by RBI
cards.back:
(D) Attachment of movable property by RBI

II.9 Recovery — Modes under S.8B-8G include attachment, sale, arrest, receiver — all on certificate issued by RPFC acting as recovery officer. RBI does not attach movables for EPFO.

cards.front:
Recovery certificate under EPF Act is issued by:

(A) RPFC / Authorised Officer
(B) District Collector
(C) CBDT
(D) Labour Commissioner ■ II.4 Applicability
cards.back:
(A) RPFC / Authorised Officer

II.9 Recovery — Authorised Officer (usually RPFC/APFC) issues certificate under S.8B. Recovery officer then executes through modes in S.8E.

cards.front:
Excluded employee under Para 2(f) of EPF Scheme is one who:

(A) Earns less than ₹6,500
(B) Has withdrawn EPF on retirement/superannuation
(C) Works less than 180 days a year
(D) Is a contract labourer
cards.back:
(B) Has withdrawn EPF on retirement/superannuation

II.4 Applicability — Para 2(f): member who has attained 58 and drawn full EPF amount is 'excluded employee'. Also: those above ₹15,000 wage at joining who don't opt in. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
The EPF Act extends to:

(A) Whole of India except J&K;
(B) Whole of India including J&K; (post Aug 2019)
(C) Only notified states
(D) Only urban areas ■ II.6 CBT Structure
cards.back:
(B) Whole of India including J&K; (post Aug 2019)

II.4 Applicability — Original S.1(2) excluded J&K.; Post abrogation of Art. 370 (Aug 2019), EPF Act extended to UT of J&K; and Ladakh from 31-Oct-2019.

cards.front:
Maximum number of employers' representatives on CBT (S.5A) is:

(A) 5
(B) 10
(C) 15
(D) 20
cards.back:
(B) 10

II.6 CBT Structure — S.5A(1)(d): maximum 10 employer representatives + 10 employee representatives (parallel 5A(1)(e)). Central Govt reps capped at 5; State Govt reps at 15.

cards.front:
Executive Committee of CBT is constituted under:

(A) S.5A
(B) S.5AA
(C) S.5B
(D) S.5C
cards.back:
(B) S.5AA

II.6 CBT Structure — S.5AA empowers CBT to constitute an Executive Committee; day-to-day work is supervised by EC.

cards.front:
A Regional Committee (RC) is constituted under:

(A) S.5AA
(B) S.5B
(C) S.5C
(D) Para 3 of EPF Scheme ■ II.7 Offences & Penalties
cards.back:
(B) S.5B

II.6 CBT Structure — S.5B constitutes Regional Committees for advising CBT on regional matters. Usually one per State/UT.

cards.front:
Offences by a company are dealt with under:

(A) S.14
(B) S.14A — every person in charge shall be liable
(C) S.14AA
(D) S.14B ■ II.5 Contributions
cards.back:
(B) S.14A — every person in charge shall be liable

II.7 Offences & Penalties — S.14A: every person in charge of and responsible for the conduct of business is deemed guilty, unless proved that offence occurred without knowledge or due diligence exercised.

cards.front:
Which RCM code applies to EPF establishment registration online?

(A) PF-01
(B) ECR 2.0 (Electronic Challan-cum-Return)
(C) PMRPY
(D) ABRY
cards.back:
(B) ECR 2.0 (Electronic Challan-cum-Return)

II.5 Contributions — ECR 2.0 (launched 2017) is the unified electronic challan-return system used by employers for monthly EPF returns.

cards.front:
Under the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY), Govt subsidised:

(A) Employer's entire 12% for new employees earning < ₹15,000 for 3 years (ended Mar 2019)
(B) Entire 24% contribution for all employees
(C) Only EDLI share
(D) Only admin charges
cards.back:
(A) Employer's entire 12% for new employees earning < ₹15,000 for 3 years (ended Mar 2019)

II.5 Contributions — PMRPY (2016-19): Govt paid 12% employer EPS+EPF contribution for new employees earning <₹15,000 — scheme ceased for new registrations after 31 March 2019.

cards.front:
ABRY (Atmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana), Oct 2020-Mar 2022, subsidised:

(A) Only employee's 12%
(B) Entire 24% for new employees earning <₹15,000 (establishments ≤1000)
(C) Only employer's 8.33%
(D) Only EDLI contribution ■ II.4 Applicability
cards.back:
(B) Entire 24% for new employees earning <₹15,000 (establishments ≤1000)

II.5 Contributions — ABRY subsidised the full 24% (both shares) for establishments up to 1,000 employees, and only employee share for larger establishments — payable for 24 months.

cards.front:
Which of the following is NOT specifically listed in Schedule I of EPF Act?

(A) Cement
(B) Biscuits
(C) Iron and steel
(D) Video editing
cards.back:
(D) Video editing

II.4 Applicability — Schedule I lists specific industries that attract EPF coverage. Video editing is NOT listed; such establishments come under general S.1(3)(b) notification.

cards.front:
EPFO's current operational jurisdiction is across how many Regional Offices?

(A) 59
(B) 92
(C) 122
(D) 150
cards.back:
(C) 122

II.4 Applicability — EPFO operates through 122 Regional Offices (as of 2025) — reduced/rationalised from earlier 135+ through reorganisation.

cards.front:
The Centralised Pension Payment System (CPPS) went live nation-wide on:

(A) 1 April 2024
(B) 1 October 2024
(C) 1 January 2025
(D) 1 April 2025 ■ II.6 CBT Structure
cards.back:
(C) 1 January 2025

II.4 Applicability — CPPS went live across all 122 ROs on 1 January 2025; benefits ~70 lakh EPS pensioners by enabling bank-account-agnostic pension disbursal.

cards.front:
The 239th CBT meeting (Feb-Mar 2026) decided on:

(A) Only administrative charges
(B) Only wage ceiling hike
(C) EPF interest rate 8.25% for FY 25-26 + PF Amnesty Scheme
(D) Only EDLI cap ■ II.5 Contributions
cards.back:
(C) EPF interest rate 8.25% for FY 25-26 + PF Amnesty Scheme

II.6 CBT Structure — 239th CBT (Feb-Mar 2026): retained EPF rate 8.25% + announced PF Amnesty Scheme for voluntary compliance and reduced damages. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
Universal Account Number (UAN) is unique to:

(A) Each establishment

Voluntary disclosure under PF Amnesty Scheme:

Employer in litigation on whether allowance is basic wages:

cards.front:
The Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) 1995 came into force on:

(A) 1 April 1995
(B) 1 August 1995
(C) 16 November 1995
(D) 31 March 1996
cards.back:
(C) 16 November 1995

III.11 EPS Applicability — EPS 1995 was notified on 16 November 1995 (retrospectively from that date) — replaced Family Pension Scheme 1971. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
EPS 1995 is mandatory for employees whose monthly wages at the time of joining are:

(A) Up to ₹6,500
(B) Up to ₹15,000
(C) Up to ₹21,000
(D) Any wage
cards.back:
(B) Up to ₹15,000

III.11 EPS Applicability — EPS applicability is governed by the wage ceiling of ₹15,000 at time of joining (raised from ₹6,500 on 1 Sep 2014). Above ₹15,000, employee may opt in with employer.

cards.front:
Government of India contributes to EPS at:

(A) Nil
(B) 1.16% of wages (up to ₹15,000)
(C) 3.67% of wages
(D) 8.33% of wages ■ III.12 Pension Formula
cards.back:
(B) 1.16% of wages (up to ₹15,000)

III.11 EPS Applicability — GoI contributes 1.16% on capped wages (₹15,000), making total EPS inflow 9.49% (of which 8.33% from employer + 1.16% from GoI).

cards.front:
The EPS pension formula is:

(A) (Pensionable Salary × Service) / 70
(B) (Average wage × Service) / 60
(C) (Basic wage × Service) / 100
(D) (Maximum wage × Service) / 50
cards.back:
(A) (Pensionable Salary × Service) / 70

III.12 Pension Formula — Monthly Pension = (Pensionable Salary × Pensionable Service) ÷ 70.

cards.front:
Pensionable Salary (Para 11) is:

(A) Average of last 12 months' wages
(B) Average of last 60 months' wages
(C) Last drawn wage
(D) Highest wage in last 5 years
cards.back:
(B) Average of last 60 months' wages

III.12 Pension Formula — Para 11(3) w.e.f. Sep 2014: average of last 60 months' wages (earlier last 12 months). Capped at ₹15,000 unless higher pension option.

cards.front:
Minimum service for EPS monthly pension is:

(A) 5 years
(B) 7 years
(C) 10 years
(D) 15 years
cards.back:
(C) 10 years

III.12 Pension Formula — Para 9: Minimum 10 years of pensionable service required for monthly pension. <10 years = withdrawal benefit under Table D.

cards.front:
If an employee's pensionable service is 25 years + pensionable salary ₹15,000, his monthly
pension will be:

(A) ₹3,570
(B) ₹5,357
(C) ₹7,500
(D) ₹10,000
cards.back:
(B) ₹5,357

III.12 Pension Formula — (15,000 × 25) / 70 = ₹5,357 per month.

cards.front:
Bonus years added for pensionable service if actual service ≥ 20 years:

(A) 1 year
(B) 2 years
(C) 5 years
(D) 10 years
cards.back:
(B) 2 years

III.12 Pension Formula — Para 10(2): 2 bonus years added to pensionable service if member has 20+ years of service.

cards.front:
Minimum monthly pension under EPS (notified Sept 2014) is:

(A) ₹500
(B) ₹1,000
(C) ₹2,500
(D) ₹3,000 ■ III.13 Types of Pension
cards.back:
(B) ₹1,000

III.12 Pension Formula — Minimum pension of ₹1,000/month was introduced w.e.f. 1 Sep 2014. Proposal to raise to ₹7,500 (2024-26) is pending — NOT yet notified.

cards.front:
Superannuation pension is payable on attaining age:

(A) 55
(B) 58
(C) 60
(D) 62

Early pension (reduced) can be taken from age:

(A) 50
(B) 55
(C) 58

(A) 25%
(B) 50%
(C) 75%

(B) 25%
(C) 50%

cards.back:
(B) 25%

Orphan pension (no surviving parent) is at:

(C) 100% of member's pension
(D) 25% of member's pension
cards.back:
(B) 75% of widow pension

(B) Withdrawal benefit under Table D
(C) Widow pension from deceased's contribution

Disability pension under EPS is payable:

cards.front:

(B) Months (post-14 Jun 2024 amendment)

cards.back:
(C) Both A and B, depending on date of leaving service

(A) Extended higher pension eligibility to all pre-Sep 2014 members who contributed on actual wages

(B) Only Table C

(B) Export quotas

(B) 30 years

(B) Not eligible

cards.front:
Fundamental accounting equation is:

(A) Assets = Liabilities + Capital
(B) Assets = Liabilities - Capital
(C) Capital = Liabilities + Assets
(D) Profit = Income - Expense
cards.back:
(A) Assets = Liabilities + Capital

IX.41 Fundamentals — Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity (Capital). Also expressed as A = L + E. Foundation of double-entry book-keeping.

cards.front:
Golden Rule for Personal Account:

(A) Debit the receiver, Credit the giver
(B) Debit all expenses, Credit all incomes
(C) Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out
(D) Debit all assets
cards.back:
(A) Debit the receiver, Credit the giver

IX.41 Fundamentals — Personal A/c — Debit the Receiver, Credit the Giver. Real A/c — Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out. Nominal A/c — Debit expenses/losses, Credit incomes/gains.

cards.front:
Real Account rule:

(A) Debit receiver / Credit giver
(B) Debit what comes in / Credit what goes out
(C) Debit expenses / Credit incomes
(D) Debit assets / Credit liabilities
cards.back:
(B) Debit what comes in / Credit what goes out

IX.41 Fundamentals — Real accounts = tangible assets (Cash, Machinery, Stock). Golden rule: Debit what comes in, Credit what goes out.

cards.front:
Nominal Account rule:

(A) Debit receiver / Credit giver
(B) Debit what comes in / Credit what goes out
(C) Debit expenses & losses / Credit incomes & gains
(D) Debit all entries
cards.back:
(C) Debit expenses & losses / Credit incomes & gains

IX.41 Fundamentals — Nominal accounts = incomes, expenses, gains, losses. Rule: Debit expenses/losses, Credit incomes/gains.

cards.front:
Double-entry system means:

(A) Each transaction affects only one account
(B) Each transaction has debit and credit effect in at least two accounts
(C) Each entry is duplicated
(D) Two books are maintained
cards.back:
(B) Each transaction has debit and credit effect in at least two accounts

IX.41 Fundamentals — Double-entry: every transaction has dual aspect — recorded as a debit in one account and a credit in another. Sum of debits = sum of credits.

cards.front:
Matching concept requires:

(A) Revenues matched with the period's expenses that produced them
(B) Cash inflows = outflows
(C) Only cash accounting
(D) Debit = Credit
cards.back:
(A) Revenues matched with the period's expenses that produced them

IX.41 Fundamentals — Matching concept: expenses incurred to earn revenue of a period are matched with that revenue in the same period — basis of accrual accounting.

cards.front:
Accrual concept means:

(A) Cash basis of accounting
(B) Revenue/expense recognised when earned/incurred, regardless of cash receipt
(C) Transactions recorded at year-end only
(D) Double-entry system
cards.back:
(B) Revenue/expense recognised when earned/incurred, regardless of cash receipt

IX.41 Fundamentals — Accrual basis recognises revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, matching them to the period — not dependent on cash flow timing.

cards.front:

(A) Going concern
(B) Consistency
(C) Accrual
(D) Conservatism ■ IX.42 Statements
cards.back:

cards.front:
Balance Sheet represents:

(A) Flow over a period
(B) Financial position at a point in time
(C) Only cash position
(D) Only profit and loss
cards.back:

IX.42 Statements — Balance Sheet is a statement of financial position at a specific date — showing assets, liabilities, and equity. P&L; is for a period.

cards.front:
Income Statement (P&L;) shows:

(A) Financial position
(B) Performance over a period (income, expenses, profit/loss)
(C) Only cash flows
(D) Only assets
cards.back:
(B) Performance over a period (income, expenses, profit/loss)

Trial Balance is prepared to:

(A) Calculate profit
(B) Check arithmetical accuracy of ledger balances
(C) Show financial position
(D) Plan cash flows

IX.42 Statements — Trial Balance lists all ledger balances to verify debits = credits. Starting point for preparing financial statements.

cards.front:
Cash Flow Statement classifies activities into:

(A) Operating, Investing, Financing (AS-3 / Ind AS 7)
(B) Revenue, Capital
(C) Direct, Indirect
(D) Receipts, Payments
cards.back:
(A) Operating, Investing, Financing (AS-3 / Ind AS 7)

IX.42 Statements — AS-3 / Ind AS 7 requires classification into three: Operating, Investing, and Financing activities. May use direct or indirect method for operating activities.

cards.front:
Depreciation is a:

(A) Cash expense
(B) Non-cash expense — allocation of asset cost over useful life
(C) Liability
(D) Income
cards.back:
(B) Non-cash expense — allocation of asset cost over useful life

IX.42 Statements — Depreciation is non-cash — a systematic allocation of the cost of a tangible asset (less residual value) over its useful life.

cards.front:
Straight-Line Method of depreciation charges:

(A) Equal amount each year
(B) Decreasing amount each year
(C) Based on usage
(D) Based on market value
cards.back:
(A) Equal amount each year

IX.42 Statements — SLM: (Cost - Scrap) / Useful Life = constant annual depreciation. Simplest and most commonly used method.

cards.front:
Written Down Value (WDV) / Diminishing Balance method charges:

(A) Constant amount
(B) Decreasing amount each year (% on opening book value)
(C) Equal to usage
(D) No depreciation ■ IX.43 Ratios
cards.back:
(B) Decreasing amount each year (% on opening book value)

IX.42 Statements — WDV method applies constant rate (%) on reducing (book) balance → decreasing charge each year. Required under IT Act for most assets.

cards.front:
Current Ratio = ?

(A) Current Assets / Current Liabilities
(B) Total Assets / Total Liabilities
(C) Liquid Assets / Liabilities
(D) Net Profit / Sales
cards.back:
(A) Current Assets / Current Liabilities

IX.43 Ratios — Current Ratio = Current Assets ÷ Current Liabilities. Ideal: 2:1. Measures short-term liquidity. # Ans

cards.front:
Quick (Acid Test) Ratio = ?

(A) Current Assets / Current Liabilities
(B) (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid) / Current Liabilities
(C) Cash / Expenses
(D) Liquid Assets / Total Assets
cards.back:
(B) (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid) / Current Liabilities

IX.43 Ratios — Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid Expenses) / Current Liabilities. Ideal: 1:1. Stricter liquidity measure.

cards.front:
Debt-Equity Ratio = ?

(A) Long-term Debt / Shareholders' Equity
(B) Current Debt / Equity
(C) Total Assets / Equity
(D) Debt / Sales
cards.back:
(A) Long-term Debt / Shareholders' Equity

IX.43 Ratios — Debt-Equity = Long-term Debt ÷ Shareholders' Equity. Indicates financial leverage. Lower = safer; higher = more leveraged.

cards.front:
Gross Profit Ratio = ?

(A) Gross Profit / Sales × 100
(B) Net Profit / Sales × 100
(C) GP / Cost
(D) Operating Profit / Net Profit
cards.back:
(A) Gross Profit / Sales × 100

IX.43 Ratios — GP Ratio = (Gross Profit ÷ Sales) × 100. Measures basic operating efficiency.

cards.front:
Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) = ?

(A) EBIT / Capital Employed × 100
(B) Net Profit / Capital
(C) Sales / Assets
(D) EPS / Price ■ IX.41 Fundamentals
cards.back:
(A) EBIT / Capital Employed × 100

IX.43 Ratios — ROCE = (EBIT / Capital Employed) × 100. Capital Employed = Total Assets Current Liabilities. Key profitability metric.

cards.front:
Conservatism (Prudence) principle says:

(A) Overstate profits
(B) Anticipate no profit but provide for all losses
(C) Ignore losses
(D) Show highest value ■ IX.42 Statements
cards.back:
(B) Anticipate no profit but provide for all losses

IX.41 Fundamentals — Conservatism: record all anticipated losses but not anticipated profits. Basis of valuing inventory at 'cost or NRV, whichever lower'.

cards.front:
Contingent Liability is disclosed:

(A) In Balance Sheet as liability
(B) As notes to accounts (off-balance-sheet)
(C) In P&L;
(D) Not at all ■ IX.41 Fundamentals

(B) As notes to accounts (off-balance-sheet)

IX.42 Statements — Contingent liabilities (possible obligations depending on future events) are disclosed as notes / footnotes, not recognised in Balance Sheet itself (AS-29 / Ind AS 37).

cards.front:
AS (Accounting Standards) in India are issued by:

(A) RBI
(B) SEBI
(C) ICAI (recommended) / MCA (notified) for companies
(D) ICSI

cards.front:
Entity concept (business entity concept) says:

(A) Business is separate from its owner
(B) All entities are equal
(C) Same accounting for all
(D) Business = owner
cards.back:
(A) Business is separate from its owner

IX.41 Fundamentals — Business Entity concept: business is a separate accounting entity distinct from its owner(s). Owner's personal transactions are NOT mixed with business.

cards.front:
Money Measurement concept requires:

(A) All transactions recorded in monetary terms
(B) Only cash recorded
(C) Non-monetary items shown separately
(D) Government currency only
cards.back:
(A) All transactions recorded in monetary terms

IX.41 Fundamentals — Only transactions expressible in monetary terms are recorded. Non-monetary items (like employee skills, management quality) are NOT recognised.

cards.front:
Going Concern assumption implies:

(A) Business will continue indefinitely
(B) Business will close soon
(C) Quick liquidation
(D) Forced sale ■ IX.42 Statements
cards.back:
(A) Business will continue indefinitely

IX.41 Fundamentals — Going Concern: entity will continue in operation for the foreseeable future — enables historical cost accounting, deferral of expenses, etc.

cards.front:
FIFO (First-In-First-Out) inventory valuation assumes:

(A) Oldest inventory is sold first
(B) Newest inventory is sold first
(C) Average cost
(D) LIFO
cards.back:
(A) Oldest inventory is sold first

IX.42 Statements — FIFO: oldest stock (first purchased) is issued first. Closing inventory reflects latest purchase prices. In inflation, gives higher profit.

cards.front:

(A) Permitted under AS-2 / Ind AS 2
(B) Not permitted (Ind AS 2 prohibits LIFO)
(C) Only used in retail
(D) Standard method ■ IX.43 Ratios
cards.back:

cards.front:
Inventory Turnover Ratio = ?

(A) COGS / Average Inventory
(B) Sales / Inventory
(C) Purchases / Stock
(D) Revenue / Debtors ■ IX.41 Fundamentals
cards.back:
(A) COGS / Average Inventory

IX.43 Ratios — Inventory Turnover = Cost of Goods Sold / Average Inventory. Higher = faster movement / efficient stock management. Measured in 'times'.

cards.front:
Suspense Account is created when:

(A) Debit = Credit in Trial Balance
(B) There is a difference in Trial Balance — to temporarily balance it
(C) Cash is lost
(D) Assets are revalued ■ IX.42 Statements
cards.back:
(B) There is a difference in Trial Balance — to temporarily balance it

IX.41 Fundamentals — Suspense A/c holds the difference temporarily until errors are located. Once all errors found, Suspense A/c should vanish.

cards.front:
In Receipts and Payments A/c (for NPO):

(A) Only revenue items recorded
(B) Only cash transactions (both capital and revenue)
(C) Only credit sales
(D) Non-cash items too
cards.back:
(B) Only cash transactions (both capital and revenue)

IX.42 Statements — Receipts and Payments A/c is a real (cash) account — records ALL cash receipts and payments, both capital and revenue nature.

cards.front:
Income & Expenditure Account for a non-profit organisation is equivalent to:

(A) Balance Sheet
(B) Profit & Loss A/c
(C) Receipts & Payments A/c
(D) Cash Book ■ IX.43 Ratios
cards.back:
(B) Profit & Loss A/c

IX.42 Statements — Income & Expenditure A/c serves as P&L; equivalent for NPOs — records revenue items on accrual basis; surplus = excess of income over expenditure.

cards.front:
Debtors Turnover Ratio = ?

(A) Credit Sales / Average Debtors
(B) Total Sales / Total Debtors
(C) Cash Sales / Debtors
(D) Sales / Creditors ■ IX.42 Statements
cards.back:
(A) Credit Sales / Average Debtors

IX.43 Ratios — Debtors Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Average Debtors (incl. B/R). Higher ratio = faster collection. Inverse: Debt Collection Period.

cards.front:
Treatment of bad debts already written off but recovered later:

(A) Credit P&L; A/c (as income)
(B) Debit P&L; A/c
(C) Reduce Debtors again
(D) No entry ■ IX.41 Fundamentals
cards.back:
(A) Credit P&L; A/c (as income)

cards.front:
Compound journal entry means:

(A) Entry with more than one debit or credit
(B) Entry in foreign currency

XV.59 Physical — India's area (~3.287 million sq km) makes it the 7th largest country in the world.

The highest peak in India is:

(B) Life insurance
(C) Motor insurance (own damage)

cards.back:
(B) Life insurance

XVI.61 Insurance — Life insurance is a contract of ASSURANCE (fixed sum assured on death), not indemnity. PYQ 2025 Q107 direct.

cards.front:
The doctrine that, after indemnification, the insurer steps into the insured's shoes to recover
from the third party is called:

(A) Subrogation
(B) Contribution
(C) Indemnity
(D) Mitigation
cards.back:
(A) Subrogation

XVI.61 Insurance — Subrogation — flows from indemnity; applies only to non-life insurance. # Ans Explanation

cards.front:
'Uberrima fides' (utmost good faith) requires:

(A) Only the insurer to disclose terms
(B) Only the insured to disclose risk
(C) Both parties to disclose all material facts
(D) Only the broker to disclose commission
cards.back:
(C) Both parties to disclose all material facts

XVI.61 Insurance — Both parties must disclose ALL material facts before contract formation. Non-disclosure voids policy.

cards.front:
Insurance in India is regulated by:

Principle of 'Causa Proxima' means:
